description: A single-panel thermodynamic plot (Ellingham-style) of standard free energy of formation versus temperature for two oxides. The x-axis is labelled "TEMPERATURE (°C)" and spans 0 to 2400 with major ticks every 400; the y-axis is labelled "ΔF° K.Cals" and spans -300 to -100 with ticks every 50. A legend in the lower-right identifies open circles as MgO and filled circles as Al2O3. The MgO (open-circle) curve falls steeply: it starts near the -275 K.Cals gridline at 0 °C, passes about -250 K.Cals near 700 °C and reaches roughly -125 K.Cals near 1900 °C. The Al2O3 (filled-circle) curve is shallower: it begins near -255 K.Cals at 0 °C, lies near -220 K.Cals around 600 °C, and ends near -130 K.Cals near 2200 °C. The two lines intersect at approximately 1600 °C, with MgO more negative (more stable) below the crossing and Al2O3 more negative above it. The figure demonstrates that in the crossing region, near 1873 K, aluminium in an Fe-Al melt can reduce MgO, causing magnesium pick-up and crucible erosion. Data points are not individually labelled with numeric values.
measured_quantities: standard free energy of formation ΔF° (K.Cals)

observations.observation: The x-axis is labelled 'TEMPERATURE (°C)' and runs from 0 to 2400 with major ticks every 400.
The y-axis is labelled 'ΔF° K.Cals' and runs from -300 to -100 with ticks every 50.
The legend identifies open circles as MgO and filled circles as Al2O3.
The MgO (open-circle) curve is the steeper of the two, starting near the -275 K.Cals gridline at 0 °C and ending near -125 K.Cals close to 1900 °C.
The Al2O3 (filled-circle) curve is shallower, starting near -255 K.Cals at 0 °C and ending near -130 K.Cals close to 2200 °C.
The MgO and Al2O3 curves intersect at approximately 1600 °C; MgO is more negative below the crossing and Al2O3 more negative above it.
The caption states the figure plots standard free energy of formation as a function of temperature of MgO and Al2O3.
The citing text asserts that Al in the melt can reduce MgO at temperatures of about 1873 K, very close to the melting point of iron aluminides, based on this standard free energy data (Fig. 2).
The citing text states that reduction of MgO leads to magnesium pick-up by the alloy and to erosion of the crucible.
No numeric values are printed on the data points themselves; values must be read against the gridlines.
